notes: Realistic developer conversations, written before the extractor was run against them.
An expected fact is a hit when one extracted fact body contains every keyword, case-insensitively.
A {{secret:<shape>}} placeholder expands to the seeded synthetic token of that shape from
eval_memory.SECRET_SHAPES, so no credential-shaped literal is ever committed to the repo.
'forbidden' lists the prefixes that must never reach an extracted fact.

messages.content: Should the daemon mirror use SQLCipher or plain SQLite? I don't want to maintain two encryption stories.
We decided to use SQLCipher for the daemon mirror because the daemon already links it, so there is exactly one encryption story to reason about.
Ten thin slice PRs landed overnight and reviewing them ate my whole morning.
Want me to batch the remaining work differently?
Yes. I prefer fewer, fatter pull requests with one theme each over ten narrow slices.
How does recall combine the lexical score with the vector score?
Hybrid mode fuses BM25 and cosine similarity with reciprocal rank fusion, and the fusion weights live in the constants header of the engine.
Fresh clone. How do I get the memory MCP tests running?
First run bootstrap-memory.sh from tools/openburnbar-mcp, then install requirements-dev.txt into the same .venv.
And the tests themselves?
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` from that directory.
Forgetting a memory left orphan rows behind. Why didn't the cascade fire?
The root cause was that SQLite disables foreign keys per connection, so ensure_schema now issues a PRAGMA on every open.
Who owns hash chain verification, the engine or the daemon?
The engine owns it: verify_audit_chain walks memory_audit on every read of the trail, and the daemon never re-verifies.
Can I stash my worktree changes before pulling?
Never run a bare git stash in a worktree here: the stash stack is shared across every worktree and another session can pop yours.
Bugbot left an approving comment. Can I merge?
No. Codex is the independent reviewer and the approval gate; Cursor Bugbot output is never approval evidence.
ollama serve dies the moment I start it on this Mac.
Known gotcha on this machine: Ollama has to run under Rosetta via arch -x86_64, otherwise the runner aborts during model load.
That fixed it, thanks.
The macOS app build is red on my PR. Do I have to fix it before merging?
The Mac app build runs nightly and is not a merge ticket; only the fast checks gate the merge door.
Can I keep an API key verbatim in a memory?
Only under secret_policy=retain, which requires the memory_secret_retain capability; without it the write is refused outright.
And where does the verbatim text end up?
In the encrypted vault table, never in the indexable body, and only get with include_secrets can open it.
Why is there a -wal file sitting next to the memory store?
The store runs in WAL mode, so writes land in the sidecar journal until a checkpoint folds them back into the main file.
What's the release ritual for the Mac app?
First bump CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION and tag the commit, then bind the owner-emergency packet to that tagged build.
Where do the credential regexes come from? I want to add one for a new provider.
They are owned by tools/project-code-memory/secret-pattern-corpus.json; the memory engine compiles that corpus at import and never defines patterns of its own.
So adding one there covers both the scanner and the memory gate?
Yes, one corpus, both consumers.
test_memory_engine only fails on my machine, and only after 5pm.
Which assertion?
The one comparing createdAt to today's date.
That is the classic one: the assertion compares a naive local timestamp against a UTC one, so it breaks when your offset pushes the date past midnight.
Your last three answers were essays.
Noted. How short do you want them?
I would rather have one accurate sentence than three paragraphs of hedging, so keep answers brief.
ruff keeps rewrapping my lines at 88 and the diff is noise.
The repo convention is line length 120 targeting py311; ruff.toml sets both and CI runs ruff format --check.
How does the MCP actually talk to the daemon?
Every mirrored write routes through a unix socket, and the daemon rejects any peer that fails first-party code-signature verification.
What happens by default when a credential shows up in something I memorize?
The secret policy defaults to redact, so the body is stored with the credential replaced by a labelled placeholder and nothing verbatim is kept.
The root cause was that the release workflow reads GITHUB_TOKEN, not DEPLOY_TOKEN, so your shell export never reached the publish step.
Local runs 401 against Anthropic but CI is green with the same key.
Where is the key set locally?
launch-memory.sh does not source .env, so the server process never sees ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; export it in the shell that starts the launcher.
It hangs because the instance profile has no STS permission, so the SDK retries the assume-role call until the socket timeout fires.
Are memories captured from a session usable straight away?
Chat-sourced memories default to review status quarantined and cannot be injected into a pack until someone approves them.
The tool list is huge and my context budget is tight.
Set BURNBAR_MCP_TOOLSET=memory and the server exposes only the corpus and memory tools; the ops profile keeps FinOps instead.
How long is the SessionEnd hook allowed to run?
It must finish inside the 30 second hook timeout, and the memorizer enforces its own 20 second deadline so it never gets killed mid-write.
If I swap the embedding model, do the old vectors still count?
No. Vectors carry an embedding version and are never compared across versions, so swapping the model forces a full re-embed.
Who should I ping about the memory MCP before I refactor it?
Alberto owns the memory MCP end to end, and the daemon mirror is maintained by the same person, so there is no second reviewer to loop in.
Can a recall pack ever blow past the token budget I hand it?
It cannot: tokensUsed measures the whole serialized pack including the envelope, and the budget floor always leaves room for one truncated line.
Can I just open openburnbar.sqlite from a Python script to check a row?
No, that file is SQLCipher-encrypted and the stdlib sqlite3 module cannot open it; reads have to go through the daemon.
thanks, that's all for today
You're welcome. Have a good evening.
